import re

text = "Hello,  World! C++ rocks!"
# Replace sequences of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen
# [^a-z0-9]+ matches one or more non-alphanumeric chars
pattern1 = r'[^a-z0-9]+'
result1 = re.sub(pattern1, '-', text)
print(f"Simple: {text!r} -> {result1!r}")

# But this gives us too many hyphens - we need to collapse consecutive ones
# Let's use a different approach - match sequences and replace with single hyphen
pattern2 = r'(?<=[^a-z0-9])[^a-z0-9]+'
result2 = re.sub(pattern2, '-', text)
print(f"With lookahead: {text!r} -> {result2!r}")

# Or better yet, match sequences within each word
pattern3 = r'(?<=[a-z0-9])[^a-z0-9]+(?=[a-z0-9])'
result3 = re.sub(pattern3, '-', text)
print(f"With lookbehind/lookahead: {text!r} -> {result3!r}")

# Let's try a different pattern - match non-alphanumeric and check if we're at word boundary
pattern4 = r'(?<=[^a-z0-9])[^a-z0-9]+'
result4 = re.sub(pattern4, '-', text)
print(f"With lookahead for any char: {text!r} -> {result4!r}")

# Actually the simplest might be to just replace all non-alphanumeric with hyphen, then collapse consecutive
pattern5 = r'[^a-z0-9]+'
collapsed = re.sub(pattern5, '-', text)
collapsed2 = re.sub(r'-+', '-', collapsed)  # Collapse multiple hyphens
print(f"Two-pass: {text!r} -> {collapsed} -> {collapsed2!r}")
